authority: Ruling 36 §1 (owner 2026-10-07): groups 1–4 signed off; text byte-identical to the Ruling 35 assumption-closure packet at 5867a864 (entry-text sha256 c67c18b829584d626ec6ca0e849c8334ffdabf837e8184b7295a571a5ef69780 equals the entry at that commit); record written at Ruling 40 step 7
text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0072"
description = "For any two distinct request bodies a preflight receipt can be about, `content_digest_sha256` produces distinct SHA-256 digest values."
justification = """
`check_unbound_receipt_is_about_this_request` accepts a preflight receipt as being about this
call only when the `sha-256-received` digest the server signed into the receipt equals the
SHA-256 digest of the body this client sent. So `client.response_binding_disposition`'s *a
receipt about another request answers nothing* is conditional on two distinct bodies not
sharing that digest, and the unit registered no premise saying so. The comparison is exact
over the encoded digest; what it cannot do is make the DIGEST injective, and a claim may not
exceed its evidence closure.

It is the second-preimage property and no stronger, and the difference is the whole argument.
The adversary does not choose this client's request body: the client composes and sends it.
What an adversary can obtain is a receipt the server signed for bytes the adversary chose and
submitted, and to have it accepted here it needs those bytes to land on the digest of a body it
was handed. That is a second preimage of a value it did not choose. This premise is therefore
deliberately weaker than collision resistance (ASM-0037) and is a per-unit entry rather than a
widening of ASM-0028, whose scope the ADR-068 Phase-1 split narrowed to the six propositions that
conclude byte agreement from digest agreement on the profile side: widening an owner-reviewed
premise would reopen assumption review for all six consumers, and none of them is this one.

Nothing here may be read as MCP-RE having proved SHA-256's second-preimage resistance, and
colliding bodies exist because the digest is not injective. The claim is computational and
deployment-scoped. It is also a BYTE binding, which this premise does not strengthen: two
transmissions of identical bytes share the digest, and that residue is why the outcome stays
`bound: false`.

It stops being acceptable if the received digest moves to a digest without SHA-256's standing,
or if the request body becomes attacker-chosen before it is sent, which would need collision
resistance and not this.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://client.response_binding_disposition",
  "boundary://boundary.crypto_primitives",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "owner-signature:asm-client-preflight-received-digest-premise (r12, 87ece9fc35fd3cf1)"
review_requirement = "Owner review; any change to the received-digest algorithm or to what it is computed over, and any change that lets the answering party choose the request body before it is sent."
premise_class = "assumed"
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "none:trusted-primitive"

authority: Ruling 40 step 6 ratified by the owner at 56aa0799, 2026-10-08, step 7 authorization
text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0076"
description = "The serving host's wall clock (`SystemTime`), as the STS and GCE/GKE metadata credential sources read it, never reads more than sixty seconds behind true UTC time, and never steps backwards by more than sixty seconds in total while a credential whose expiry it stamped is in use, so the sixty-second refresh margin those sources keep ahead of an expiry absorbs it; a clock further behind makes an expired credential read as current."
justification = """
The STS and GCE/GKE metadata credential sources judge an issued credential's remaining lifetime
against the host's wall clock: the expiry the issuer stated is compared with `SystemTime::now()`
to decide whether the credential is still usable or must be re-exchanged. THM-0117 states that
the expiry is never EXTENDED — not by the reuse floor, and not by a stated value past the session
ceiling — and that statement is about the comparison. Whether the comparison is made against the
present is this premise.

It is not ASM-0057. That premise states what the serving path hands each verifier operation, and
a credential source is not a verifier operation: it reads the clock for itself, at its own
moments, to manage a credential this proxy presents rather than one it judges.

Each source re-exchanges a credential sixty seconds before its expiry
(`CREDENTIAL_REFRESH_MARGIN`, `TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN`), so a clock behind true time by less than
that still stops using the credential no later than its true expiry. Two kinds of expiry are
compared: an absolute one the issuer stated (STS `Expiration`), which needs the reading to be
near true time, and one this host stamped as a reading plus a stated lifetime (the metadata
server's `expires_in`, and the bounded reuse floor), which needs the clock not to step back
across the credential's use. The premise states both. A clock further behind
makes an expired credential read as current, and one ahead discards a current one early; the
first is the security failure. Nothing in this repository can detect either from one reading.

It stops being acceptable if a credential source judges a lifetime against anything other than
the host wall clock, gains a clock of its own, or keeps a refresh margin below sixty seconds.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://proxy.aws_sts_credentials",
  "unit://proxy.gcp_kms_adapter",
  "unit://proxy.gcp_metadata_token_lifetime",
  "unit://proxy.aws_web_identity_credential_exchange",
  "boundary://boundary.clock",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 RERE-RATIFICATION §4b P-1 (Ruling 40 step 4)"
review_requirement = "Owner review if a credential source's lifetime is judged against anything other than the host wall clock, or its refresh margin falls below sixty seconds."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The DEPLOYMENT OPERATOR's host clock discipline (NTP or equivalent), across the `SystemTime::now()`
readings the STS and metadata credential sources take: no reading is behind the current UTC time
by more than sixty seconds, and the clock does not step backwards by more than sixty seconds in
total while a credential whose expiry it stamped is in use.
"""

tool_specific_mechanism = "none:trusted-seam"

[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0079"
description = "`Instant` is monotonic and advances at true rate while the process runs."
justification = """
The trust plane's resolution window and reload cadence are measured on `std::time::Instant`: a
cached key's authority ends at its first-caching instant plus the window `T` (THM-0097), and a
reload is due a cadence after the last one. Those are DURATIONS, which is why they are not on
the wall clock — and a duration means something only if the monotonic clock never goes back and
advances at the rate time does. A clock that stalls keeps a cached answer authoritative past
`T`; that is the failure that matters here.

It is not a wall-clock premise and is not implied by one: a monotonic clock is trusted to
advance, not to agree with any peer.

It stops being acceptable if either window is measured on anything but the monotonic clock.
"""

  "unit://proxy.trust_reload_cadence",

]

boundary_owner = """

readings never decrease, and their differences track elapsed real time while the process runs.

[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0084"
description = "After MCP-RE has successfully completed `sync_all` on a newly created manifest-floor marker file and successfully completed `sync_all` on the directory containing it, the host filesystem and storage preserve that marker and its contents across process or host failure."
justification = """
THM-0121 says a manifest version the client has accepted and recorded is not lost to a power
loss. `persist` (`mcp-re-client-proxy/src/manifest_floor.rs`) creates the marker, calls `sync_all`
on the file, then calls `sync_all` on the directory containing it, and reports success only after
both have returned. That ORDER, and that the directory sync is also made when the marker already
exists, are this project's and are tested (`an_equal_version_record_still_establishes_durability`,
`an_already_existing_marker_still_syncs_the_directory`). What a `sync_all` that returned success
guarantees — that the marker and its directory entry survive a crash of the process or the host —
is the filesystem's and the device's, and nothing here can establish it: a filesystem mounted
with write barriers off, or a device that acknowledges a cache flush it did not perform, returns
success and loses the marker.

It stops being acceptable if the manifest-floor directory is placed on storage whose `sync_all`
does not survive host failure, or if `persist` is ever changed to report success before both
syncs have returned.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://client.manifest_floor",
  "boundary://boundary.manifest_floor_filesystem",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 6 (owner ruling on THM-0121, Option A)"
review_requirement = "Owner review if the floor's durable-record step changes, or if the floor directory may be placed on storage without a durable `sync_all`."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The host kernel and the filesystem and device holding the manifest-floor directory, across
`sync_all` on a marker file and on its directory: once both have returned success the marker and
its contents persist across a process or host failure.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0085"
description = "When MCP-RE decodes input through `ciborium` as a CBOR value, or through `coset` as a COSE_Sign1, and the decode succeeds, the decoded CBOR values correspond to the values the input bytes encode, and the decoded protected headers, unprotected headers, payload and signature are those the input bytes represent, with the protected and unprotected headers kept distinct. The `Sig_structure` that `coset` builds from such a decoded COSE_Sign1 for a signature check is the RFC 9052 section 4.4 encoding over the protected-header bytes exactly as received, and the external AAD and payload passed to it."
justification = """
THM-0041 reads a Signed Statement and a Receipt off the wire through `coset::CoseSign1` and
`ciborium`, and then reasons about what is in them: the algorithm and the claims it reads come
from the PROTECTED header, a receipt's position commitment comes from the protected header, and
its inclusion proof from the unprotected one. That the decoded structure is the one the bytes
encode, with the two headers not mixed, is the libraries' and nothing here establishes it.

The second sentence is for one conjunct: the Signed Statement's own COSE `Sig_structure` verified
under a key resolved for its issuer kid, and the same for the receipt's signature. MCP-RE does not
construct those signed bytes. `verify_cose_sign1_with_payload` hands `coset` a verifier callback and
`CoseSign1::verify_signature` / `verify_detached_signature` build the `Sig_structure` that is passed
to it. MCP-RE chooses the key, the algorithm check (`require_alg`) and, for a detached receipt, the
payload it re-derived.

Every refusal MCP-RE owns is NOT in this premise and is tested here: a non-empty or unknown `crit`,
an `iss` that is not the signing `kid`, a second occurrence of a CWT claim, trailing octets after
the statement's payload and after an inclusion proof, a repeated key in the `vdp` map, an unsupported
verifiable data structure, a leaf index outside the tree, and a root that is not a tree hash.

It stops being acceptable if SCITT evidence is decoded through another library, or if the signed
structure is ever built by this project instead of by `coset`.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_statement_attribution",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_receipt_shape",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_algorithm_agreement",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_position_commitment",
  "boundary://boundary.cose_cbor",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 6 (owner ruling on the coset/ciborium premise)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the `coset` or `ciborium` dependency, or to how SCITT evidence is decoded or its signed structure is built."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The `ciborium` and `coset` crates, across a successful decode of CBOR input and of a COSE_Sign1,
and across the construction of the `Sig_structure` for a signature check from a decoded COSE_Sign1.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"
